name: Postscript
summary: SMS marketing for Shopify stores: campaigns, automations and opt-in tools.
best_for: Shopify stores with a list large enough that SMS beats email on response: the per-message economics only work once volume justifies the platform fee
skip_if: you are testing whether SMS works for you at all: the $49 minimum spend on the free tier means the experiment has a floor before you have sent a single message, and the listed rates cover the US and Canada only
honest_knock: The $0 a month is not free: it carries a $49 monthly minimum spend, which means $49 is your floor whether you send anything or not. Read the tiers as what they are: a platform fee plus a per-message rate plus carrier fees. That third line is easy to miss because it sits in a footnote rather than on the tier cards, and it is not small: the page puts the average US carrier fee at $0.00435 an SMS and $0.00832 an MMS (read 17 November 2026), so against the $0.009 SMS rate on Starter it adds close to half again. Before you compare this with anything, work out your monthly message volume and multiply it out on all three published tiers: Growth costs $100 more than Starter but saves a tenth of a cent per SMS, so on text alone it pays back at about 100,000 messages a month, and on picture messages, a cent and a half cheaper, at about 6,700.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on postscript.io/pricing and on the App Store listing apps.shopify.com/postscript-sms-marketing, and in our own test session on 17 November 2026; first read 2026-08-30) Starter is $0 a month with a $49 monthly minimum spend at $0.009 per SMS and $0.045 per MMS. Growth is $100 a month at $0.008 per SMS and $0.03 per MMS, and Professional is $500 a month at $0.007 per SMS and $0.024 per MMS; all three add carrier fees. Enterprise is contact sales. The introductory SMS rates we read on 30 August and 19 September 2026, $0.015 on Starter and $0.01 on Growth before the volume rate, are gone from both pages: the pricing page and the listing now print one SMS rate per plan. Carrier fees are asterisked on every tier and quantified in a footnote: average US carrier fees of $0.00435 per SMS and $0.00832 per MMS, and $0.0047 per text RCS message and $0.0087 per media RCS message, with the listed rates covering the US 50 states and Canada only. The pricing page now heads the plans SMS and RCS, and Enterprise lists an option to add RCS. The free trial is a credit equal to $100 against message and carrier fees during your first 30 days, on every plan on the listing, and Growth and Professional also show a 30 day free trial there; exhaust the credit and you are billed at the Free package rate unless you select another package. Phone numbers are priced outside the tiers: a dedicated toll free number is assigned and verified free of charge at install, while a dedicated short code costs $750 a month levied by the carriers and passed on without markup. No contract is required. The same page sells a separate Postscript AI Plan at $699 a month with per message rates from $0.003 to $0.30 depending on the product and message type, through sales. In our own test session the onboarding asked for a billing address and then a phone number, an account email and acceptance of Postscript's terms before it would continue, so we did not reach a plan or payment screen.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the start of Postscript on a Shopify development store: the permissions, a page that stayed on Loading Postscript, an onboarding with three Not Found toasts, a billing address (made up test data) and a second step that asked for a phone number, an own e-mail address and consent to the terms, with Continue greyed out. No campaign or popup was made and nothing was sent. No plan or payment screen was reached, so all prices come from the listing and not from a test. Install: the install button on the App Store listing (English) was used in our own tab at 18:24; it led through a page of the vendor (the pay page of Postscript) to the Shopify dialog Install app, which asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the app permissions were approved. After that the vendor page app.postscript.io/shopify/auth stayed on Loading Postscript for more than 20 seconds. Postscript did not appear in Settings, Apps (the list showed 8 other apps), so it is not known whether the install was completed; it may only finish after the onboarding, or the auth step failed. Onboarding: through the login address of the vendor for the store the onboarding did open: Welcome to Postscript! (step 1 of 10), with three toasts Not Found and a promo popup about syncs with another e-mail tool that was closed without accepting anything. Continue first gave a modal Add a billing address (Country/region, Address line 1, City, State/province, Postal code); made up test data was entered (an address in Austin, Texas) and saved, and no card was asked. Step 2 of 10, Contact information, asked for First name, Last name, Phone number and Email address (Use an email only you control. You'll use it to access your account.), a box to receive text updates, a required box to agree to the terms of service and a box for marketing e-mails of Postscript. Continue stayed greyed out. Core action, a draft SMS campaign or sign-up popup: NOT reached. The set-up needs a phone number, an own e-mail address for a separate Postscript account and consent to the terms before any campaign screen, and nothing of that was entered, so nothing was sent, no number was bought or verified and no campaign or popup was made. Time to the block: about 2 minutes (18:24 to about 18:26), with no result. Plans (from the listing, NOT a test result): the App Store listing of 17 Nov says Starter is Free to install with a $49 monthly minimum spend and a $100 credit for the first 30 days, then $0.009 per SMS and $0.045 per MMS plus carrier fees; Growth is $100 a month with $0.008 per SMS, $0.03 per MMS and a 30-day free trial; Professional is $500 a month with $0.007 per SMS, $0.024 per MMS and a 30-day free trial; all charges are billed in USD. Difference with the dossier (from the listing, not from the app): the dossier gives Starter as $0.015 per SMS and then $0.009, and the listing names only $0.009 (after the credit); the other amounts are the same. This was not checked in the app because the plan screen was not reached. Checkout: NOT reached. No Shopify approval screen and no plan screen were seen, no card was entered and nothing was approved or paid. Cancelling: not tested. Postscript was not in Settings, Apps, so there was nothing to uninstall. Not tested: a campaign, the sign-up popup, the plans and the payment screen, the cancellation route, a sender number, 10DLC and TCPA registration, and a short code. Clean up: no uninstall was needed (Postscript was not in the app list at about 18:28); the made up billing address was saved in the vendor onboarding and nothing else was entered; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app stayed on Loading Postscript after the permissions and was not in the app list; the onboarding showed three Not Found toasts; a billing address was asked before step 2; and step 2 of 10 needed a phone number, an own e-mail address for a separate account and consent to the terms before anything could be tried.
